basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 24.' and it opens 'VERS. 24.-- Iste est Ana, qui invenit aquas calidas in solitudine, cum pasceret asinos'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 24.-- Iste est Ana, qui invenit aquas calidas in solitudine, cum pasceret asinos Sebeon patris sui. Judaei asserunt quod iste Ana nepos Esau equarum greges in deserto ab asinis fecerit primus ascendi, ut mulorum inde nova contra naturam animalia nascerentur. Onagros quoque ad hoc admissos esse ad asinas, et ipsum istiusmodi reperisse | concubitum, ut velocissimi ex his asini nascerentur. Industria quippe humana diversum animal in coitu coegit, sicque adulterina commistione genus aliud reperit, sicut et Jacob contra naturam colorum similitudines procuravit.
